functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Most inferior of the deep hip external rotators; flat quadrilateral shape gives it the largest PCSA of the short rotator group despite the group's collectively small individual muscle bellies.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

trigger_points.location_description: Short, flat muscle belly deep in the posterior hip, spanning from the lateral ischial tuberosity to the intertrochanteric crest
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: A vague, deep ache in the buttock and hip, sometimes radiating to the posterior thigh or knee
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Walking, especially downhill or on stairs, and activities loading hip external rotation/stabilization
trigger_points.notes: Frequently mistaken for piriformis syndrome or sciatica because of overlapping deep buttock/posterior hip referral; can also be mistaken for patellofemoral pain when referral reaches the knee
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual (Travell JG, Simons DG, Simons LS, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 2: The Lower Extremities, 1st ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1992; Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019) -- as cited in learnmuscles.com, 'Quadratus Femoris: The Unusual Suspect Behind Gluteal Pain' (https://learnmuscles.com/blog/2026/05/11/quadratus-femoris-the-unusual-suspect-behind-gluteal-pain/)
